prompts.mainfig_stages: Use case: scientific-educational. Create an original high-resolution wide clean academic tutorial infographic for a Chinese paper-writing website, three equal panels in one horizontal row on white background. Crisp vector-like raster diagram, very large readable sans-serif labels, no decorative characters. Title: 'Mainfig: content → layout → emphasis'. This is a hypothetical design illustration, not measured evidence. Panel 1 heading '1 CONTENT': four spacious cards labeled 'Question + documents', 'Direct answer', 'Check evidence', 'Supported / unresolved'. These are an inventory, no arrows. Panel 2 heading '2 LAYOUT': two precisely aligned horizontal routes. Shared left label 'Question + documents'; upper route labeled 'Baseline' goes to 'Direct answer'; lower route labeled 'Proposed' goes through 'Check evidence' to 'Supported / unresolved'. Show real reading-direction arrows only, upper and lower output aligned, leave enough room, monochrome graphite lines and white cards. Panel 3 heading '3 ENCODING': exactly repeat the two routes from panel 2 with all objects and connections unchanged. Only 'Check evidence' and its outline use teal emphasis, ordinary input and output cards white with dark outline. Under it small short legend: 'Teal: added operation'. No check marks, success icons, scores, performance curves, or causal improvement assertions. Keep each panel compact with abundant clean space, panel separators subtle pale grey; actual labels all large and spelled verbatim, no overlapping lines/text. Prefer a 3:1 wide 3000px-ish figure. The route labels Baseline / Proposed are grey and consistent. Show the improvement as adding a design step, never as proven efficacy.
prompts.framework_stages: Use case: scientific-educational. Create an original high-resolution wide three-panel academic tutorial diagram on white background, large readable sans-serif text, clean flat vector-like style. Title 'Framework: dependencies → layout → roles'. Hypothetical evidence QA design, no real results. Three panels equally spaced, heading '1 DEPENDENCIES', '2 LAYOUT', '3 ROLES'. Each panel contains EXACTLY the same directed dependency graph: 'Question + documents' → 'Retrieve' → 'Check evidence' → 'Answer'; from 'Answer' arrow to independent 'Evaluator'; 'Reference answer' only points into 'Evaluator', NEVER to any model or generation module. Panel1 uses a plain compact monochrome diagram with graph topology clear. Panel2 same contents arranged into top generation row left-to-right four cards, lower separate evaluation row with Evaluator and Reference answer, Answer sends down to Evaluator. Dotted large grouping outline labeled 'Generation'; distinct separate grouping outline labelled 'Evaluation'. Panel3 exactly same organized graph as panel2, with roles shown redundantly: input 'Question + documents' dashed border pale blue; intermediate operations neutral white cards except 'Check evidence' in teal emphasis; 'Answer' solid border; evaluator-only 'Reference answer' double border pale gold; 'Evaluator' neutral dark outline, all textual labels. Small legend: 'Dashed: input | Solid: output | Double: evaluation only'. Only input/output/evaluation-material roles use those borders; ordinary operation boxes are neutral. No arrows returning to generation, no hidden leakage, no celebratory check marks, no performance statistics. Use very few words, not dense prose, huge legible labels, sufficient whitespace. Exact edges and identical node list across panels matter more than ornaments. Wide 3:1 image.
